rules.ET-P-SEL-01: documented scope of each ENISA affected-asset selector clause
rules.SI-I-SEL-01: resolution of selectors against the SI's variant graph

source.document: ENISA Space Threat Landscape 2025, Annex C Table 17 (pp.85-95), column 'Affected assets', as transcribed in v2/data/legacy_v1/enisa_threats_tuple.csv
source.reliability: the transcription's own note: affected-asset text approximate (segments reliable); Annex C itself defines none of the asset terms, so every asset-class reading below is a documented interpretation

policy: Selectors stay symbolic at ET/ETP level; they are resolved only against the selected SI and its variant graph G.
An asset resolves only when its node's segment is named by the component and, for non-wildcard components, its class is the component's class or a descendant.
Attacker-scoped nodes are never affected assets.
A selector clause absent from this file is unresolved, never guessed.
Parenthesised member lists narrow the scope to the listed members; parenthesised attributes (antenna, SLE/SDL protocol) are aspects of the host asset and do not narrow it.

Ground.basis: assumed: ENISA segment name equals the architecture node segment of the same name

Space.basis: assumed: ENISA segment name equals the architecture node segment of the same name

User.basis: assumed: ENISA segment name equals the architecture node segment of the same name; current G variants model no User nodes

Human Resources.basis: assumed: no G variant models people; the segment exists only for completeness
